title: Phase 2 gap analysis input: converging record-shape standards for the logging/evidence theme
author: narko4u
summary: The phase 2 mapping exercise maps policy instruments to common themes. One cluster of instruments (EU AI Act Art 12/19/26(6), China TC260 agent guidelines, Singapore's agentic framework, SOC 2, PCI DSS v4.0.1, ISO/IEC 42001) shares a theme: automatic, tamper-evident logging of ag...
inline_text:
The phase 2 mapping exercise maps policy instruments to common themes. One cluster of instruments (EU AI Act Art 12/19/26(6), China TC260 agent guidelines, Singapore's agentic framework, SOC 2, PCI DSS v4.0.1, ISO/IEC 42001) shares a theme: automatic, tamper-evident logging of agent activity. That theme is usually stated as an outcome ("logging required"), which leaves a wide gap between what an instrument demands and what a deployer can check.

That gap is closing from an unexpected direction. Three standards bodies are now specifying the record shape itself, which turns the theme from an outcome into a checkable artefact:

- ISO/IEC 24970 (AI system logging) is in final ballot (2026-08-28), joint JTC 1/SC 42 and CEN-CENELEC JTC 21.
- prEN 18229-1 (AI Trustworthiness Framework, Part 1: Logging) is the CEN twin, public hearing closed 2026-08-20, with a normative reference relationship to ISO/IEC 24970.
- IETF draft-sharif-agent-audit-trail (Agent Audit Trail), updated 2026-09-05, defines a JSON record structure with mandatory fields and explicitly maps to the EU AI Act, SOC 2, ISO/IEC 42001, ISO/IEC 24970, prEN 18229-1 and PCI DSS v4.0.1.

Strikingly, the three converge on the same shape: hash-chained, timestamped, tamper-evident records; pre-execution capture of denials and escalations; a recording-independence gradient (an agent should not be the sole recorder of its own high-trust actions); optional external timestamp anchoring; and, in the newest revision, metadata for decision reproducibility.

A suggestion for the phase 2 mapping: include emerging standards in the instrument set, not just regulations. They are where "logging" becomes machine-checkable, and they give the gap analysis a concrete conformity anchor for the evidence theme: a deployer can now be asked not only "do you log" but "does your record match the converging shape". That distinction (self-reported telemetry versus independently attestable records) is the line regulators and auditors will draw first.

Happy to contribute a draft theme card for this cluster: instruments, the shared requirement set, and the standards now defining the checkable shape, formatted for the group's extraction prompts. Concepts only, no implementations.
